architecture: GptOssForCausalLM: 36 decoder layers, every layer an MoE block (128 routed experts, top-4, softmax over the selected 4 router logits, no shared expert; expert MLP = gated SwiGLU with alpha 1.702 and clamp limit 7.0, biases on every projection), attention alternates sliding_attention (window 128) and full_attention (18 + 18 layers, starting with sliding), GQA 64q/8kv x head_dim 64 (q width 4096 != hidden 2880), learned per-head attention sinks, YaRN RoPE (theta 150000, factor 32, original context 4096, max_position_embeddings 131072), RMSNorm, untied lm_head, vocab 201088 (tokenizer length 200019)
params_note: total parameters as instantiated by transformers (meta device; expert weights are fused bf16-shaped 3-D tensors) = the HF API safetensors total (116,829,156,672 = U8 114,661,785,600 expert weights stored as packed mxfp4 + BF16 2,167,371,072); verified equal. Vendor: 117B total / 5.1B active.
active_params_note: computed from the meta model: non-expert parameters without the input embedding table (a lookup) but with the lm_head matmul + top-4/128 of the routed expert parameters = 5,132,849,472; counting the input embedding table too (the GLM-card convention) gives 5,711,982,912 (5.71 B). The vendor quotes 5.1B active, which matches the first count.
dtype_note: checkpoint dtypes per the hub metadata: U8 (packed mxfp4 blocks and scales of the expert weights) and BF16 (attention, router, norms, embeddings, lm_head, expert biases); config.json has no torch_dtype

quantization.quantised: MoE expert weights only: mlp.experts.gate_up_proj and mlp.experts.down_proj, stored as <name>_blocks + <name>_scales (uint8); 114,661,785,600 weights = 98.1% of all parameters
quantization.kept_in_bf16: config.quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert = [model.layers.*.self_attn, model.layers.*.mlp.router, model.embed_tokens, lm_head]; norms and the expert biases are bf16 too
quantization.requirements_for_packed_path: CUDA/XPU device with compute capability >= 7.5 + Triton >= 3.4.0 + `kernels` package (Mxfp4HfQuantizer.validate_environment, transformers 4.57.6, read). pip: `kernels` (PyPI 0.18.3 on 2026-11-22, python >= 3.10); torch 2.8.0 pins triton==3.4.0 on Linux x86_64 (PyPI metadata), so the torch-2.8.0 pod image of sbx/RUNBOOK.md has Triton, and sbx/RUNBOOK.md section 2 now adds `kernels` for gpt-oss keys (without it transformers silently dequantises to bf16)
quantization.fallback: dequantise to bf16 (logged as a warning) when a requirement is missing, on CPU, or with use_kernels=True; the two paths run different expert kernels (Triton matmul_ogs on the packed weights vs the dense bf16 loop/bmm of GptOssExperts), so do not mix packed and dequantised runs inside one experiment
quantization.noise_consequence: the expert weights are quantised (uint8 blocks / scales, or Triton-wrapped), not float: sbx.noise.WeightNoise with its default selection raises QuantizedParamError (docs/noise.md; the real model was not loaded here); use include=sbx.noise.INCLUDE_ATTN (attention projections only: 955,514,880 parameters = 0.82% of the model). Activation noise is unaffected.

download_gb_note: sum of the 15 HF-format model-*.safetensors shards at the repo root (65,248,893,184 B = 60.77 GiB), which is all that from_pretrained fetches; the repo also holds the same weights twice more (original/*.safetensors, the reference implementation, and metal/model.bin): see download_gb_full_repo
download_gb_full_repo_note: everything in the repo (195,764,040,609 B). huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(repo) WITHOUT ignore_patterns=['original/*', 'metal/*'] fetches all of it: so the RUNBOOK downloads with ignore_patterns=['original/*','metal/*'] (a plain snapshot_download needs a much bigger disk than 2 x download_gb + 50)
weights_gb_4bit_note: NOT an NF4 estimate: for this family the native mxfp4 checkpoint size (~4.5 bits per parameter overall); no bitsandbytes path was tested
weights_gb_note: decimal GB. weights_gb_bf16 = 2 x params_b = what transformers materialises if it DEQUANTISES the mxfp4 experts (see quantization.fallback); the native packed size is checkpoint_gb / download_gb / weights_gb_4bit_est
weights_gb_loaded_note: ~66 GB resident at idle on one H100 SXM 80GB with the HF transformers path (reported by the lead, not re-measured here)
fits_single_80gb_detail: YES, with the native mxfp4 weights: 65.25 GB of HF-format safetensors; ~66 GB resident at idle on one H100 SXM 80GB with the HF transformers path (reported by the lead, not re-measured here), which leaves ~19.6 GB (arithmetic: 85.58 GB usable on an 80 GB card - 66 GB) for the KV cache and activations; batch generation with the core.batches budgets works there (reported by the lead). Packed mxfp4 path (kept in 4 bits) needs ALL of: a CUDA (or XPU) device with compute capability >= 7.5, Triton >= 3.4.0 and the `kernels` package; the MoE Triton kernels are then fetched from the hub repo kernels-community/triton_kernels at load time (so the pod needs hub access or a populated kernels cache). If any is missing, transformers 4.57.6 (quantizers/quantizer_mxfp4.py, read) logs a warning and DEQUANTISES the experts to bf16 (233.66 GB for this model); a CPU-only load always dequantises; use_kernels=True also forces dequantisation. The bf16 fallback (233.66 GB) cannot fit one 80 GB card (>= 4 x 80 GB or offloading). Scope: this is the GENERATION path (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run); direction building (Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats) has its own budget, see direction_building_memory.

direction_building_memory.applies_to: sbx.core.Ctx.hidden_last and Ctx.neutral_stats (every sbx.dirs recipe). Both run ONE full forward over the whole prompt with output_hidden_states=True and without logits_to_keep (GptOssForCausalLM.forward defaults to logits_to_keep=0 = all positions, read), so all num_layers+1 hidden-state tensors AND the logits of every prompt position are alive at once. Generation (Ctx.gen / Ctx.run) is not affected: generate() keeps no hidden states and computes last-token logits.
direction_building_memory.formula: bytes per prompt token = (num_layers + 1) * hidden_size * 2 + vocab_size * 2 (bf16 hidden states and logits). A LOWER bound (ESTIMATE, not a GPU measurement): the KV cache (config.use_cache=true, so forward(use_cache=None) builds one: +36864 B/token for the 18 full-attention layers), the O(T^2) eager attention matrix (see eager_attention_peak_gb) and MoE transients come on top. sbx batching caps a hidden_last batch at 14000 prompt tokens.
direction_building_memory.free_gb_basis: 79.7 GiB usable on an 80 GB card (85.58 GB) minus the ~66 GB resident at idle reported by the lead

longest_pool_prompt.basis: evals.get_pool() (wmdp + hard + nonbio: 1174 questions on 2026-11-22, after the evals MAX_PROMPT_CHARS=7500 filter), this key's tokenizer and adapter.build, framings N and E

longest_unfiltered_hard_prompt.basis: data/hard/*.jsonl as read before the evals filter (968 questions, framing E); this question is no longer in any pool, the raw file still has it

eager_attention_peak_gb.basis: ESTIMATE: GptOssPreTrainedModel._supports_sdpa = False, so attention runs eager (or a flash backend with sink support): eager_attention_forward materialises [batch, 64 heads, T, T] attention weights (bf16, + concatenated sink column + softmax copies), 64 * T^2 * 2 B per copy for ONE sequence. core.batches() budgets this (0.16 x free memory) except for a single over-budget prompt, which still runs alone.

direction_building_memory.fits_flags_note: fits_longest_* follow the other cards' arithmetic (hidden states + logits only); the *_incl_eager_attention flags add 3 copies of the eager attention matrix (ESTIMATE) and are the practical verdict

accessible_with_local_token_note: the repo is public and ungated: no token is needed, and the access check below was made without one

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info(files_metadata=True, token=False) + HTTP HEAD with no credentials on config.json (redirects followed => 200) and the first HF-format safetensors shard (redirect NOT followed: 302 = redirect to the CDN); nothing downloaded
access_check.cached_files_identical_to_hub: config.json, chat_template.jinja, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, special_tokens_map.json (git/LFS object ids compared with the hub's)

license_notes: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file and model-card tag license:apache-2.0) plus a short USAGE_POLICY file asking users to comply with applicable law
min_transformers_note: the gpt_oss model code AND the mxfp4 quantizer first appear in the transformers 4.55.0 wheel (absent from 4.54.1: checked from both wheels); config.json says transformers_version 4.55.0.dev0; only 4.57.6 was actually run here
thinking_note: hidden chain of thought in the harmony `analysis` channel is always generated; 'Reasoning: low|medium|high' in the system turn sets how much (vendor: fast / balanced / deep); the template has no switch to turn it off
max_new_note: sbx default for gpt-oss (adapter.max_new): the hidden reasoning AND the final answer must fit. The lead reports that about 28% of wmdp_cyber outputs have no final answer at 800 (cut inside the analysis channel; reported from the H100 run, not re-measured here): check parse_rate and nofinal_rate of baseline N on every eval before reading a steering effect
layer_path_note: attribute path starting at the loaded model object, i.e. adapter.layers(model) = model.model.layers (base class default)

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(real hub config.json from the local HF cache) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device); the parameter count of the meta model equals the HF API safetensors total exactly. The 1-based convention, the active-hook behaviour and left-padded batching were checked on a tiny random GptOssForCausalLM (4 layers, hidden 64, 4 experts, sliding_window 8, vocab 201088) with the REAL gpt-oss tokenizer and sbx.adapters.gptoss.GptOss through sbx.core.Ctx, transformers 4.57.6, CPU, in a scratch script (NOT part of sbx/tests: no test file covers the gptoss adapter or these cards)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)
layer_path_verified.config_source: official repo config.json (local HF cache; same blob as the live revision)
layer_path_verified.hidden_states_under_active_hooks: output_hidden_states returns each layer's output as forward() produced it, i.e. BEFORE forward hooks run: with core.Hooks adding a vector at layer 2, hidden_states[2] equals the UNSTEERED value while hidden_states[3] and the logits change, and an own forward hook registered after Hooks.__enter__ sees unsteered + vector. Mechanism: transformers.utils.generic.check_model_inputs monkey-patches module.forward of the GptOssDecoderLayer (_can_record_outputs) and stores its return value. Read post-intervention activations with your own hook, never from hidden_states.
layer_path_verified.batched_decoding: greedy generation of 5 prompts of 107-224 tokens (sliding window 8 < prompt length, sinks, left padding, fp32) gave identical tokens one by one and in one left-padded batch; bf16 / GPU numerics and the real checkpoint were not tested here

kv_note: bf16 bytes. core_formula = sbx.core.kv_bytes_per_token(model) = 2 x 36 x 8 x 64 x 2 (every layer counted as full attention, so core.batches over-budgets). true (long sequences) = 18 full-attention layers x 2 x 8 x 64 x 2 per token PLUS a constant 4,681,728 B per sequence for the 18 sliding-window layers, which keep only sliding_window - 1 = 127 tokens in HF's DynamicSlidingWindowLayer (verified on the tiny model: kv length 7 for window 8). For sequences shorter than ~128 tokens the two agree.
est_max_batch_note: ESTIMATE from sbx.core.batches() with free memory 19.6 GB (85.58 GB usable - 66 GB loaded), 300-token prompts and max_new 800: bound by the 14000-token budget (46 sequences), not by KV or prefill attention; at 160-token prompts the cap of 64 applies. Not measured.

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured with the REAL gpt-oss tokenizer (offline cache) + adapter.build (real harmony chat template, date pinned) over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions); N = no framing text, E = instructed-sandbagging developer text. The fixed harmony system block alone is 61 tokens of every prompt (+6 for the user / assistant wrappers, +7 for a developer turn). by_set_N: mean / p95 / max prompt tokens (framing N) of the harder eval files in data/hard/ (unfiltered raw files).

est_tokens_per_question_basis: ESTIMATE, NOT measured (no weights/GPU here): hidden reasoning at effort low plus a one-letter final answer; max_new=800 caps it. The only handed-over data point is the lead's report that ~28% of wmdp_cyber outputs hit the 800 cap without a final answer, which implies a mean of at least ~300 tokens on that eval. Replace with the measured mean generated length of the first full run: np.percentile([ctx.ntok(t) for t in res.texts], [50, 90, 99]).
est_runtime_note: NOT measured: no throughput number exists for this key (no GPU here; none was handed over). The lead reports that batched generation with the core.batches budgets works on one H100 SXM 80GB for gptoss-120b.
estimates_unmeasured: est_tokens_per_question, est_tokens_range, est_max_batch_80gb_prompt300, direction_building_memory.free_gb_after_weights (for 20b) and every eager-attention figure are ESTIMATES / arithmetic. Verified: parameter counts, config, layer path, hook behaviour, template rendering, token counts, hub sizes.

special_tokens.bos_note: defined by the tokenizer but NEVER rendered by the harmony template; the prompt starts with <|start|>
special_tokens.generation_eos_note: generation_config.json: <|return|> 200002, <|endoftext|> 199999, <|call|> 200012; <|end|> (200007) is NOT a stop token

checkpoint_key_check.method: keys of model.safetensors.index.json (fetched, metadata only) vs the meta-device state_dict of the real config, transformers 4.57.6
checkpoint_key_check.difference: 72 extra checkpoint keys = per layer the fused expert tensors gate_up_proj / down_proj are stored as *_blocks + *_scales (Mxfp4HfQuantizer.update_expected_keys maps them); every other key matches

reported_behaviour.source: NOT measured for this card. 120b items: sbx/SPEC.md section 1 (earlier project runs: gpt-oss-120b, mxfp4, reasoning effort low, greedy, 4-10-option MCQ, written answers; results/ was not re-read) and the lead's H100 SXM 80GB runs of 2026-11-22
items: SPEC section 1, quoted: 'Instructed sandbagging is strong: WMDP-bio 84.7→30.5; mentions the instruction in ~50% of reasoning; stays silent in the rest.'
SPEC section 1, quoted: 'consequence-note framing (no instruction) does not change accuracy (WMDP 88.7 vs 87.5, GPQA-bio 65.4 vs 65.4)'

SPEC section 1: direction B (mean over flipped questions of h_E - h_N, layer 15) restores accuracy under E when subtracted with alpha 0.8 U (WMDP 30→78) but costs ~10-37 pts of generic accuracy; random directions at that alpha collapse the model to 0%
reported by the lead: refusals ('I’m sorry, but I can’t help with that.') appear under consequence-style framings
reported by the lead: about 28% of wmdp_cyber outputs have no final answer at max_new=800

known_issues: hidden_states under active hooks: HF records the layer outputs BEFORE forward hooks run (verified on a tiny GptOssForCausalLM, transformers 4.57.6: hidden_states[L] stays unsteered while the hooked layer's own output and everything downstream change). Never read output_hidden_states while steering hooks are active; attach your own capture hook AFTER core.Hooks.__enter__ to observe post-intervention activations (SPEC section 1).

mxfp4 loading: the packed path needs compute capability >= 7.5, Triton >= 3.4.0 and the `kernels` package (kernels-community/triton_kernels is fetched from the hub at load time); if one is missing transformers falls back, with only a logged warning, to dequantising the experts to bf16 = 233.66 GB, which does not fit one 80 GB card. Check the load log for the dequantisation warning and torch.cuda.memory_allocated() after load.

weight noise (known issue handed over by the lead; docs/noise.md derives it from the public config and a uint8 mimic, the real quantised model was not loaded here): the expert weights are quantised (uint8 *_blocks / *_scales, Triton-wrapped after swizzling), not float tensors, so sbx.noise.WeightNoise with the default selection raises QuantizedParamError (refused loudly on purpose). Use the attention-only selection include=sbx.noise.INCLUDE_ATTN (955,514,880 parameters = 0.82% of the model) and record that weight-noise cells perturb attention only; activation noise is unaffected.

refusals: under consequence-style framings the model sometimes answers 'I’m sorry, but I can’t help with that.' instead of a letter (reported by the lead). core.score treats that as unparsed = wrong, so it lowers accuracy exactly like a wrong answer. Count refusals separately (cells.jsonl refusal_rate, nofinal_rate, acc_answered; docs/analysis_plan.md 'Refusals vs wrong answers'): a refusal is not sandbagging, and a gain that is only fewer refusals is not hidden capability.

parser history (verify before trusting old cells): until 2026-11-22 the base-class parser read the refusal 'I’m sorry, but I can’t help with that.<|return|>' (and 'I cannot ...') as option I (index 8) whenever the question had 9 or 10 options (I checked this on GptOss.parse_letter with the original rule: None for <= 8 options, 8 for 9-10). Affected evals: the 9-10-option questions of mmlupro_bio, mmlupro_nonbio and supergpqa_bio, all of medxpertqa_text and 2 labbench_litqa2 questions. Such a refusal counted as the answer 'I' (right iff 'I' is correct), was parsed=True and so was invisible to refusal_rate. sbx/adapters/base.py now rejects letters that start a sentence (label_follows / classify_lead; re-checked: GptOss.parse_letter returns None for the refusal at 4, 9 and 10 options), but cells that were run before the fix on those evals are contaminated: re-run them or exclude refusal-heavy conditions. Re-check with GptOss().parse_letter('I’m sorry, but I can’t help with that.<|return|>', 10) is None.

truncation: max_new=800 cuts about 28% of wmdp_cyber outputs before the final channel (reported by the lead). split() then returns (text, ''), the answer is unparsed, parse_rate drops and accuracy is understated; any steering that shortens the reasoning looks like a gain (control (c) of docs/analysis_plan.md catches this as FORMAT_ARTIFACT). Read parse_rate and nofinal_rate next to every accuracy; raise max_new (e.g. 1200-1600) for hazard-adjacent control evals if their baseline parse rate is low.

disk: from_pretrained fetches only the 65.25 GB of HF-format shards, but a plain huggingface_hub.snapshot_download('openai/gpt-oss-120b') (what a naive pre-download does; sbx/RUNBOOK.md section 2 now passes ignore_patterns) fetches the whole repo, 195.8 GB, because original/ and metal/ hold the same weights again; pass ignore_patterns=['original/*', 'metal/*'] (or download only the shards).

date pinning: the chat template injects today's date; GptOss.render rewrites it to 2025-08-05. Prompts rendered through another path (tok.apply_chat_template directly) carry the real date and are not comparable.

reasoning effort: 'Reasoning: low' is the adapter default (SPEC section 1); Framing.effort overrides it per framing but is not validated (any string is rendered). No framing in sbx/framings.py sets effort. The vendor describes the levels as fast / balanced / deep analysis, so the amount of reasoning (and with it max_new pressure and accuracy) differs by level: never compare cells run at different efforts.

N has no developer turn while every instructed framing adds one ('# Instructions' header): a framing effect is partly a structure effect; the placebo framings (neg_placebo*) exist to control for this.

greedy decoding: generation_config.json ships do_sample=true (no temperature / top_p; the model card gives no sampling advice); sbx forces do_sample=False. With bf16 and top-4 MoE routing, answers can depend on batch composition (expected, NOT measured here): sbx.run's N2 rerun (reversed order) measures that floor and analyze.py control (d) uses it.

attention is eager (_supports_sdpa = False): memory grows with T^2 per sequence (direction_building_memory.eager_attention_peak_gb: ~89 GB of attention matrix alone for the 26k-token labbench_cloning prompt that the evals filter removed; ESTIMATE).

HF KV accounting: core.kv_bytes_per_token assumes every layer keeps all tokens, but the sliding-window layers keep 127 (see kv_note); core.batches therefore over-budgets KV for long prompts (conservative, harmless).
recommended_gpu: 1x 80 GB (H100 SXM 80GB used by the lead: ~66 GB resident at idle, ~19.6 GB left for KV cache + activations) with Triton >= 3.4.0 + `kernels` installed so that the experts stay mxfp4; without them HF dequantises to bf16 (233.7 GB: >= 4 x 80 GB). Direction building (Ctx.hidden_last, up to 14000 prompt tokens per chunk) needs ~8.6 GB for hidden states + logits on top (see direction_building_memory); an H200 (141 GB) is comfortable. Whether the Triton mxfp4 kernels run on pre-Hopper cards (A100) was not verified here.
greedy_only_note: sbx decodes greedily (do_sample=False in core._gen_chunk); the repo's generation_config.json says do_sample=true and the vendor gives no sampling recommendation, so nothing is lost by greedy decoding.
